messages.content: I need to set up a Baltimore client trip for Sunday, September 30 through Tuesday, October 2. The kickoff is Monday afternoon and Tuesday's workshop ends at 4:30. I can leave Minneapolis after 2:00 Sunday. Nothing is booked.
What part of Baltimore is the client office near, and what limits should I use for airfare and hotel? Also, are you open to Washington-area airports if the timing or fare is materially better?

The office is near the Inner Harbor. Airfare needs to stay at or below $650 round trip, and the hotel cap is $245 a night before tax for two nights. Yes, compare the Washington airports, but account for the transfer rather than just showing a cheaper fare.

For the outbound, I would target arrival by about 9:00 p.m. Sunday so the ground trip stays manageable. For Tuesday, a 4:30 finish makes BWI departures around 6:30 p.m. or later realistic; DCA should be about 7:30 or later, and IAD about 8:00 or later. Does the workshop end at the same Inner Harbor office, and will you have a checked bag?
Same office, carry-on only. I can leave directly at 4:30, but I don't want a schedule that depends on everything going perfectly.

That favors BWI. From the Inner Harbor, allow roughly 25-40 minutes by car in ordinary traffic, plus a buffer; DCA is more often 60-90 minutes, while IAD can take 75-110 minutes. Rail can reduce cost, but it adds a station transfer and is less attractive immediately after the workshop.
What flight windows look workable from MSP? I don't need exact flight numbers yet.

The strongest structure is a Sunday nonstop leaving MSP in the mid-to-late afternoon and reaching BWI in the early evening, then a Tuesday nonstop leaving BWI after 6:30 p.m. A current comparison also shows viable one-stop combinations through Chicago or Detroit, but they use more of Sunday and provide little savings. Comparable MSP-DCA itineraries can fit under $650, though the safer Tuesday choices leave after 7:30 p.m. MSP-IAD is the weakest fit because of the longer transfer and later return requirement.
Give me a practical price comparison, including what the airport transfer does to it.

Indicative round-trip economy totals are about $470-$560 through BWI, $430-$520 through DCA, and $410-$500 through IAD. From the Inner Harbor, budget approximately $30-$50 each way for BWI rides, $75-$110 each way for DCA, and $95-$140 each way for IAD. Public transit can be cheaper, especially via Baltimore Penn Station for DCA, but takes longer and adds handling. Once transfers are included, BWI is generally equal to or cheaper than the Washington options.
Agreed. Keep BWI as the working airport. What hotel areas can meet the cap without making Monday or Tuesday awkward?

Look first in Inner Harbor, Harbor East, and downtown just north of the harbor. Inner Harbor puts many offices within a short walk; Harbor East is typically a 10-20 minute walk or brief ride; downtown can be good value but should be checked block by block. Current two-night candidates are showing around $189-$239 before tax in Inner Harbor and roughly $205-$245 in Harbor East. Federal Hill is also workable, though crossing the harbor adds a little time.
Narrow that to the best overall setup. I would rather not spend the full hotel cap just to move a few blocks.

The best structure is an Inner Harbor or nearby downtown hotel around $205-$225 per night before tax, within about a 10-minute walk of the office. That preserves the lodging budget without creating a daily ride requirement. I would only move to Harbor East if the room is similarly priced or clearly better for the same rate.
Summarize the schedule and budget we should use for the next search. Don't reserve anything yet.

Working plan: fly MSP-BWI nonstop on Sunday, September 30, departing after 2:00 p.m. and preferably arriving by 8:30-9:00 p.m. Stay two nights near the Inner Harbor, targeting $205-$225 per night before tax and never exceeding $245. On Tuesday, leave the client office at 4:30 p.m. for BWI and use a nonstop departure no earlier than 6:30 p.m., with 7:00 p.m. or later providing a better buffer. Expected airfare is roughly $470-$560, plus about $60-$100 total for airport rides. DCA and IAD are not worth the added transfer time at the currently indicated savings. No reservations have been made.
